name: Belgium
tagline: Cheap, excellent, and mostly not in English at bachelor level
summary: Belgium is two higher education systems in one country. Dutch-speaking Flanders (KU Leuven, Ghent, Antwerp, VUB, Hasselt) and French-speaking Wallonia and Brussels (UCLouvain, ULB, Liege, Mons) each have their own ministry, fees, rules and calendar. Tuition for an EU student is among the lowest in western Europe - 1,181.40 EUR for a full year in Flanders in 2026/27 - and the universities are genuinely strong. The honest problem for an IB student from Denmark is language: almost all Belgian bachelor's degrees are taught in Dutch or French, and the fully English-taught bachelor's offer is small. Master's programmes are a different story, with hundreds in English.
whyConsider: Very low EU tuition: 1,181.40 EUR for a full 60-credit year in Flanders in 2026/27, and a means-tested scale from 0 to 1,194 EUR in French-speaking Belgium.
KU Leuven, Ghent and UCLouvain are among the oldest and most research-intensive universities in continental Europe.
Brussels is the centre of EU institutions, which makes it an unusually good base for politics, law, economics and international relations - and for internships.
Open access for most programmes: if your diploma is recognised and you meet the language requirement, you enrol. There is no points race.
Living costs are moderate by western European standards - Study in Flanders puts a student month at roughly 800-1,000 EUR including 450-600 EUR rent.
watchOuts: English-taught bachelor's are rare. Flemish law restricts English-taught bachelor programmes, and most of what you will find in English at bachelor level sits at university colleges or in a handful of specific programmes. Check that the exact programme exists in English before you build a plan around Belgium.

Medicine and dentistry are closed by examination. Flanders runs a competitive entrance examination sat in early July, and French-speaking Belgium runs a ranked concours in late August, with a hard cap on non-resident students.

Your diploma must be recognised before you can enrol, and the two communities do this differently: NARIC-Vlaanderen in Flanders, the equivalence service of the Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles in the south. Start it early - these procedures take weeks and have their own deadlines.
From 2026/27 the French-speaking community replaced its flat minerval with a four-tier means-tested scale, so what you pay depends on a grant assessment you have to apply for.

Deadlines are set by each institution, not nationally. KU Leuven's recommended bachelor deadline for EEA citizens for 2026-2027 was 1 June; others differ. There is no single Belgian closing date to remember.

ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: Belgium does not publish a national IB conversion. Flanders requires a secondary education diploma that gives access to university study in the country where it was awarded, plus a declaration from your school confirming that. A full IB Diploma satisfies this in principle, but recognition is decided case by case by NARIC-Vlaanderen or by the institution. Specific programmes (engineering, sciences, medicine) set their own subject expectations and will look at your HL choices.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: No published IB-to-Belgian grade conversion was found on an official source during this research. Belgian bachelor entry is normally about eligibility and language rather than a ranked score, with the exception of the medicine and dentistry entrance examinations.
notes: Flanders: Study in Flanders states that most qualifications obtained abroad do not grant direct admission and are assessed individually, so allow time for the equivalence or admission decision.

French-speaking Belgium: an equivalence decision for your foreign secondary diploma is normally required before enrolment, handled by the Direction de la reconnaissance des diplomes etrangers of the Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles. The exact deadline and fee could not be confirmed on an official page during this research - contact the service directly and start in spring 2027 at the latest.
Because Belgian enrolment often runs into September, the July release of IB results is usually not a problem - unlike the medicine entrance exams, which you sit before or just after results.

portal.name: None - you apply to each institution directly

deadlines.label: KU Leuven - recommended bachelor application deadline, non-EEA citizens
deadlines.notes: Published as "1 March" with no year. Non-EEA applicants need the earlier deadline to allow time for the visa procedure.

deadlines.label: KU Leuven - recommended bachelor application deadline, EEA citizens
deadlines.year: 2026-2027 entry - 2027-2028 dates to be confirmed on the KU Leuven application-windows tool
deadlines.notes: Published as "1 June" with no year. KU Leuven publishes deadlines through an interactive tool where you select academic year, nationality and programme. Some programmes close earlier. Verify your exact programme rather than relying on the general date.

deadlines.label: Flanders - entrance examination for medicine and dentistry (toelatingsexamen arts en tandarts)
deadlines.year: The 2026 session was reported as 2 July 2026; the 2027 date had not been confirmed on the official exam site at the time of research
deadlines.notes: Recorded only as "early July" — no 2027 date is published, so none is recorded here. Compulsory for anyone who wants to study medicine or dentistry in Flanders. Registration opens months in advance and the exam is competitive, not just a pass/fail hurdle. Re-check toelatingsexamenartstandarts.be from late 2026. The 2026 date was read from secondary reporting rather than confirmed on the official exam site.

deadlines.label: French-speaking Belgium - concours d'entree en medecine et dentisterie (ARES)
deadlines.year: The 2026 session was reported as 27 August 2026 at Brussels Expo, with registration 18 May to 5 July 2026; the 2027 dates were not published at the time of research
deadlines.notes: Recorded only as "late August" — no 2027 date is published, so none is recorded here. A ranked competitive examination, not a pass mark. Non-residents compete for a capped share of the places. The 2026 dates were read from secondary reporting rather than confirmed on the ARES site - verify at ares-ac.be and mesetudes.be.

deadlines.label: Enrolment closing date at most Belgian institutions
deadlines.year: General rule - confirm with the institution
deadlines.notes: Published as "late September to 31 October depending on institution and decree". Belgian enrolment traditionally runs late compared with the Netherlands or Ireland, but international applicants who need a diploma equivalence or a visa are given much earlier application deadlines. Do not rely on the late date.

steps: Decide which community you are applying to - Flanders (Dutch-speaking) or the Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles (French-speaking). The rules, fees and calendars are different.
Confirm on the institution's own site that the programme you want is genuinely taught in English at bachelor level.
Start the diploma recognition or admission procedure early: NARIC-Vlaanderen or the institution's admissions office in Flanders, the Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles equivalence service in the south.
Prove English at the level the programme asks for - Study in Flanders gives B2 (IELTS 6.0 overall, TOEFL iBT 72-94) as the usual minimum for bachelor's, with C1 for some programmes.
Apply directly to the institution by its own deadline (for KU Leuven, 1 June for EEA citizens in the 2026-2027 cycle).
If you want medicine or dentistry, register for the entrance examination in the relevant community as soon as registration opens - this is a separate process with its own hard deadline.
Once admitted, enrol, pay the tuition fee and arrange a room, and register with the local commune after you arrive.
application.selectionNotes: Most Belgian bachelor's are open access: meet the diploma, equivalence and language conditions and you are in, with no ranking on grades. The big exceptions are medicine and dentistry, which are closed by entrance examination in both communities. In French-speaking Belgium a further group of programmes - physiotherapy, veterinary medicine, speech therapy, and psychological sciences with a speech-therapy focus at universities, plus physiotherapy, speech therapy and audiology at university colleges - restricts non-resident students to a quota (30% of the previous year's enrolment, 20% for veterinary medicine) and allocates those places by random draw when demand exceeds the quota. For medicine and dentistry in that community, 30% of those who pass the entrance exam can be non-residents. Non-EU students only count as 'residents' in narrow circumstances such as five years of prior residence in Belgium; a Belgian address alone is not enough.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Limited. Belgium teaches its bachelor's degrees overwhelmingly in Dutch (Flanders) or French (Wallonia and Brussels), and Flemish legislation restricts how much of a bachelor programme may be taught in another language. A realistic expectation is a few dozen fully English-taught bachelor programmes nationwide, concentrated in business, international relations and some university-college programmes. The English-taught offer widens dramatically at master's level. No official count of English-taught bachelor programmes was verified during this research.
language.englishProof: Study in Flanders states that English at level B2 is required for most bachelor's and master's programmes, which it puts at IELTS 6.0 overall or TOEFL iBT 72-94 (paper 510-559), with C1 for some specialised programmes. Institutions decide individually whether an IB Diploma taught in English counts as proof - many accept IB English A or B at a specified grade, but you must confirm this with the institution.
notes: You can complete an English-taught programme without Dutch or French, but daily life, student jobs and internships will be much easier with the local language. Brussels functions in French first, with Dutch and English widely spoken.
Many Flemish universities offer free or cheap Dutch courses to their international students; take one in the first year.
If you are open to studying in French, the offer in Wallonia and Brussels is enormous and the tuition is very low. That is a genuine option for an IB student who took French B HL.

tuitionEuEea.value: Flanders: 1,181.40 EUR for a full-time year of 60 credits in 2026/27 (University of Antwerp publishes this as 305.40 EUR fixed plus 14.60 EUR per credit; Study in Flanders gives the same 1,181.40 EUR figure for EEA nationals). French-speaking Belgium: a four-tier means-tested scale from 2026/27 - 0 EUR for grant holders, 374 EUR for students of modest means, 835 EUR for the intermediate category and 1,194 EUR at the full rate.

tuitionNonEu.value: Flanders: 5,300-12,000 EUR per year for most programmes, and 8,800-25,000 EUR at schools of arts (Study in Flanders). At the University of Antwerp the increased rate is 1,000 EUR plus 55 EUR per credit, i.e. 4,300 EUR for 60 credits. KU Leuven's increased tuition fee for non-EEA citizens was reported as 9,493.90 EUR for 60 credits in 2026-2027.

costs.applicationFee: Varies by institution; several Flemish universities charge non-EEA applicants an application fee. No single national figure was verified during this research.

livingCostMonthly.value: 800-1,000 EUR per month in Flanders, of which accommodation is 450-600 EUR. Brussels is more expensive than Leuven, Ghent or Antwerp.
livingCostMonthly.year: Year not stated on the source page - figures retrieved September 2026

notes: The French-speaking community's move to a means-tested minerval in 2026/27 is new. What you pay depends on submitting a student grant application to the Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles (allocations-etudes.cfwb.be) - if you do not apply, expect to be charged the full rate.
Fees in Flanders are built from a fixed component plus a per-credit component, so a part-year or reduced study programme costs less.

funding: Danish SU taken abroad is the main source of support for a Danish student - apply to Uddannelses- og Forskningsstyrelsen before you leave.

Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles study grant (allocation d'etudes): applying is what determines which of the four minerval tiers you pay, so submit the application at allocations-etudes.cfwb.be even if you expect to pay the full rate.
Flemish study grant (studietoelage) is available to students who meet Flemish residence and means conditions; a student newly arrived from Denmark will usually not qualify in year one.
Institutional scholarships are limited at bachelor level in Belgium and are mostly aimed at non-EEA students or at master's level.

Student jobs: Belgium has a specific low-tax student contract (jobstudent) with an annual hour allowance, which makes part-time work worthwhile. Confirm the current annual hour limit before you sign a contract.
workRights: As an EU citizen you may work in Belgium without a work permit. Belgium has a special student employment contract (jobstudent) with reduced social security contributions up to an annual hours ceiling; that ceiling is set by federal law and changes, so check the current figure with the institution or the federal employment service. Non-EU students holding a student residence permit may work a limited number of hours per week during term and full time in holidays, subject to their permit conditions. No official page confirming the current hour limits was successfully retrieved during this research.
residency: As an EU citizen you do not need a visa. You must, however, register with the commune (gemeente / commune) of your Belgian address within the first months of your stay, showing your passport or ID card, proof of enrolment, proof of sufficient means and health cover. The commune issues a residence document and a national register number, which you need for a bank account, a phone contract and a student job. Non-EU students need a student visa (type D) obtained before travelling and must register with the commune on arrival.
housing: Much easier than the Netherlands or Ireland, but not effortless in Leuven, Ghent and Brussels. Belgian student rooms are called kot (Flanders) or kot/chambre (French-speaking) and are usually rented from private landlords on a ten- or twelve-month contract, with university housing services running their own listings. Start looking in spring for September, and expect 450-600 EUR a month per Study in Flanders. Brussels has more supply than Leuven but a wider quality range; Ghent and Antwerp are comfortable student cities with real turnover in the market. University housing offices publish vetted listings and are the safest place to start.
healthcare: Bring your European Health Insurance Card from Denmark. If you stay for a full degree, Belgium will normally expect you to join a Belgian health insurance fund (mutualité / ziekenfonds) - registration is cheap, sometimes free for students, and it is what makes reimbursement of GP and hospital costs work in practice. Universities usually have a designated fund they work with and will help you sign up during enrolment. Non-EU students must show proof of health cover to get their residence permit.

institutions.name: KU Leuven
institutions.englishBachelors: A small number, including Business Administration and European Studies; most bachelor's are in Dutch
institutions.note: The oldest Catholic university in the world and consistently the highest-ranked in Belgium, in a town where students outnumber everyone else.

institutions.name: Ghent University
institutions.englishBachelors: Very limited at bachelor level; extensive at master's
institutions.note: A large, research-heavy university in one of the most liveable student cities in Europe; almost everything at bachelor level is taught in Dutch.

institutions.name: University of Antwerp
institutions.note: Publishes its tuition arithmetic transparently (305.40 EUR plus 14.60 EUR per credit for EEA students in 2026-2027) and sits in Belgium's commercial capital.

institutions.name: Vrije Universiteit Brussel
institutions.englishBachelors: A handful, including social sciences and business routes shared with Vesalius College
institutions.note: The Dutch-speaking university of Brussels, secular and explicitly international, with the widest English offer of the Flemish universities at undergraduate level.

institutions.name: Hasselt University
institutions.note: Small and young, with a strong reputation for teaching quality and a much lower cost of living than the big student cities.

institutions.name: UCLouvain (Université catholique de Louvain)
institutions.englishBachelors: Essentially none - bachelor teaching is in French
institutions.note: The largest French-speaking university in Belgium, in a purpose-built car-free university town; a serious option only if you can study in French.

institutions.name: Université libre de Bruxelles
institutions.englishBachelors: Essentially none at bachelor level; some English master's
institutions.note: Brussels' French-speaking university, free-thinking in tradition and close to the EU quarter; from 2026/27 its minerval follows the new four-tier means-tested scale.

institutions.name: University of Liège
institutions.note: The only public university in Wallonia, with the region's veterinary school; its medical faculty runs the community entrance examination information for candidates. Checked 2026-09-23: ULiège's English home page has been withdrawn and now redirects to the French one, so the main site here is the French one. Individual English pages still exist further in, including the enrolment page recorded as its admissions link.

institutions.name: University of Mons
institutions.note: A small French-speaking university in a compact Walloon city, known for engineering and for translation and interpreting.

institutions.name: Vesalius College
institutions.englishBachelors: Fully English-taught bachelor's in business, international affairs and communication
institutions.note: Founded with VUB, this is one of the few places in Belgium offering an entirely English-taught, American-style liberal arts bachelor's - but it charges private-college tuition rather than the public EU rate. Checked 2026-09-23: it has not existed under its own name since February 2021, when it merged with the Institute for European Studies to form the Brussels School of Governance. vesalius.edu now redirects to a one-paragraph notice of that merger, and the degrees are taught, awarded and advertised as Brussels School of Governance BA programmes. The links here are the school's own. Its published IB line is 27 points with no specific subjects required.

institutions.name: Karel de Grote University of Applied Sciences and Arts
institutions.englishBachelors: Several English-taught bachelor's, including business and multimedia routes
institutions.note: One of the few Flemish institutions with a clearly signposted English-taught bachelor application route.

institutions.name: Thomas More University of Applied Sciences
institutions.englishBachelors: Several English-taught bachelor's in business and technology
institutions.note: The largest Flemish university of applied sciences, practice-oriented with compulsory internships, and one of the more realistic English-taught bachelor routes in Belgium.

institutions.name: Howest University of Applied Sciences
institutions.englishBachelors: Digital Arts and Entertainment is taught in English
institutions.note: Its game development programme is internationally known and taught in English, which makes Howest an outlier in the Belgian bachelor landscape.

institutions.name: Odisee University of Applied Sciences
institutions.note: A large applied-sciences institution across Brussels and Flanders, useful if you want a practical degree with a Brussels base.
